Search terms for this lesson“how do I wire my sword swing and fireball attacks onto the boss?”Guided build

Your player already fights in two ways: close-up melee with KeyCode.E (attackBox + currentEnemy) and ranged shots with KeyCode.Space (PlayerProjectile). Today you make sure both cleanly register hits on your boss prototype and produce unmistakable visual feedback.

Break It Down~10 minGuided build

Make both player attacks — your sword swing (E) and your fireball (Space) — damage your boss prototype reliably.

First, before any code: cut that into parts small enough that you could look each one up on its own.

  1. Check both melee (KeyCode.E) and ranged (PlayerProjectile) against the bossMelee checks currentEnemy populated by OnTriggerEnter2D() for "Enemy", while ranged fires PlayerProjectile tagged to collide with "Enemy" triggers and call ChangeHealth().Read: 4.6 (melee attackBox + currentEnemy) & 3.5 (PlayerProjectile)
  2. write this partRead: the KeyCode.E and PlayerProjectile damage call in the walkthrough below (ChangeHealth(-1))

If your boss still uses EnemyController.cs, KeyCode.E and PlayerProjectile already hurt it out of the box! If you created a separate BossController.cs (so you can customize phase logic), your player attack code needs to check whether the target carries EnemyController OR BossController so swings never throw a NullReferenceException.

Your turn

Look at PlayerController.cs line 114: currentEnemy.GetComponent<EnemyController>().ChangeHealth(-1);. What error occurs if you put a brand-new BossController on your boss without updating that lookup?

Look at PlayerController.cs lines 73-93 (attackBox.transform.position = ...): why does placing the boss hitbox offset along xDirection/yDirection matter when standing right next to a large boss sprite?

In the Editor ~20 min
  1. Select your Boss prefab/object in the Hierarchy: make sure it has a 2D collider marked Is Trigger tagged Enemy large enough for attackBox (on Player) and PlayerProjectile to reach cleanly.
  2. Inspect PlayerController's Inspector on your Player prefab: confirm Attack Box and Projectile are both assigned and not None.
  3. Test standing left, right, and below the boss while pressing E and Space: confirm facing aims your projectile correctly even in platformer scenes (remember in Platformer, pressing J does not set facing — only horizontal/vertical axis movement updates facing!).
Why did my melee swing miss an enlarged boss? Check how attackBox detects targets on your Player! In PlayerController, OnTriggerEnter2D() only updates currentEnemy the frame a trigger enters. If your boss also has a solid collider pushing the player backward before attackBox overlaps the boss trigger, enlarge the outer Enemy trigger or step back out and back in cleanly.

Socratic: Balancing Two Player Verbs

  1. In PlayerController.cs, melee (E) and shooting (Space) share the same cooldownTimer = .5f;. How could changing fireball cooldown vs melee damage encourage the player to dash in close instead of camping in a corner?
  2. If your boss only takes damage on a tiny glowing weak spot collider instead of its whole body, what happens when a careless Space shot hits the armored shell?
  3. What feedback (Console log, brief white sprite tint, particle burst, audio pop) proves in a quarter-second playtest that a shot actually hurt the boss rather than getting absorbed?
In the CodeGuided build

The question this answers“how do I wire my sword swing and fireball attacks onto the boss?”

You are editing Assets/Scripts/PlayerController.cs. Check your melee branch inside PlayerController.cs (KeyCode.E) and your projectile trigger inside PlayerProjectile.cs. Fill in the safe BossController fallback so hits never throw a null reference, whether your boss uses EnemyController or BossController.

This build leaves 1 line for you to write. Everything around it is given, so you always know the shape of what you are producing.

Step 1Keep directional attackBox placement and cooldown

In PlayerController.Update(), xDirection and yDirection position attackBox relative to transform.position and set facing. Both melee (KeyCode.E) and shooting (KeyCode.Space) share cooldownTimer.

        cooldownTimer -= Time.deltaTime;

        if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.E) && cooldownTimer < 0 && currentEnemy != null)
        {
            EnemyController enemy = currentEnemy.GetComponent<EnemyController>();
            if (enemy != null) { enemy.ChangeHealth(-1); }
            else { ____.GetComponent<____>()?.ChangeHealth(____); }

        }
  1. 1Counts down your 0.5-second shared attack cooldown every frame.
  2. 3Runs only on the frame E is pressed, when cooldown has expired, and OnTriggerEnter2D() has captured a target in currentEnemy.
  3. 5Tries to fetch EnemyController first (returns null without crashing if this target uses BossController).
  4. 6Hurts normal enemies (or bosses built directly on EnemyController) by 1.
  5. Your turn7If the target in currentEnemy does NOT carry EnemyController, look up BossController safely and deal 1 point of damage.Reach for GetComponent<T>(), BossController, and the hurt sign from EnemyController.ChangeHealth().Safe lookups turn crashes into clean dispatch. Earlier currentEnemy.GetComponent<EnemyController>().ChangeHealth(-1) assumed every "Enemy" carried EnemyController. Checking != null handles both ordinary grunts and custom bosses.
  6. 8Resets the half-second attack cooldown.

Step 2Check Boss hurt visual feedback inside ChangeHealth()

Add a quick white/red hit flash on the boss SpriteRenderer inside ChangeHealth(int amount) so every melee swing or fireball gives unmistakable instant feedback during prototyping.

    public void ChangeHealth(int amount)
    {
        health += amount;
        print("Boss HP: " + health);
        if (health <= 0)
        {
            Die();
        }
    }
  1. 1Reuses the exact method signature from EnemyController (int amount where -1 hurts).
  2. 3Updates current boss HP.
  3. 4Temporary prototype log so you can verify damage numbers in Console even before adding a boss UI bar.
  4. 5Triggers defeat once HP reaches zero.
  5. 7Spawns the drop/reward and ends the fight.
Check your work: the finished filetry every gap first — then open this to compare

Do the exact same two-component check inside PlayerProjectile.cs (OnTriggerEnter2D()) so both Space fireballs and E swings damage your boss identically!

// ------------------------------------------------------------------
//  REFERENCE FILE — Assets/Scripts/PlayerController.cs
//  Written to be read, not pasted. Build it with the walkthrough
//  above, one step at a time, then open this and compare.
//  If it is sitting in your project unchanged, that is the thing
//  to go and do now — the walkthrough is still above you.

// Inside PlayerController.Update() — supporting both EnemyController & BossController:
        cooldownTimer -= Time.deltaTime;

        if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.E) && cooldownTimer < 0 && currentEnemy != null)
        {
            EnemyController enemy = currentEnemy.GetComponent<EnemyController>();
            if (enemy != null)
            {
                enemy.ChangeHealth(-1);
            }
            else
            {
                BossController boss = currentEnemy.GetComponent<BossController>();
                if (boss != null)
                {
                    boss.ChangeHealth(-1);
                }
            }
            cooldownTimer = .5f;
        }

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Damage your boss reliably with both KeyCode.E melee and KeyCode.Space fireballs
  • Support BossController alongside EnemyController without null reference errors
  • Confirm directional facing and trigger overlaps work from both left and right sides of the boss
  • Verify visible hit feedback so every landed attack reads immediately
  • Commit and push
